build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Creatures march autonomously: they emerge from an entrance hatch, walk in a straight line, turn at walls, fall off ledges, and continue marching without player input. The stream is continuous at a configurable release rate. Score 0 if creatures are static, player-controlled directly, or do not march autonomously.

Jobs can be assigned by clicking a creature and selecting from a toolbar: at minimum digger (carves downward through terrain), builder (constructs diagonal staircase), and blocker (becomes impassable wall redirecting others). Each job visibly changes the creature's behavior immediately. Score 0 if fewer than 3 job types work or jobs have no effect.

Terrain is destructible and constructible: diggers remove terrain tiles creating downward passages, builders add terrain tiles creating upward staircases. Modified terrain persists and affects all subsequent creature pathing. Score 0 if terrain cannot be modified or modifications do not affect pathing.

Win and loss conditions are enforced: a save quota specifies how many creatures must reach the exit door. The level succeeds when quota is met and fails when too many creatures have died to hazards for quota to be reachable. Results are shown with retry navigation. Score 0 if there is no quota, no exit, or no failure condition.

At least 5 distinct job types exist: digger, builder, blocker, climber (scales vertical walls), and at least one more (floater for safe falls, bomber for area destruction, or miner for horizontal digging). Each has unique behavior and visual identity. Score 0 if fewer than 3 job types exist.

The campaign contains at least 12 levels with different terrain layouts, hazard placements, entrance/exit positions, and required job combinations. Levels are grouped into difficulty tiers. Score 0 if fewer than 4 levels exist.

Environmental hazards create variety: at minimum pits, liquid pools (water/lava), mechanical traps (saws, crushers), and height-based fall damage. At least 3 distinct hazard types appear across levels. Score 0 if no hazards exist beyond simple pits.

Job supplies are limited per level and vary by level design: some levels give many diggers but no builders, forcing specific strategies. The toolbar shows remaining counts that deplete as jobs are assigned. Score 0 if all jobs are unlimited or supply does not vary between levels.

Level readability is clear: terrain, hazards, entrance hatch, exit door, marching creatures, and assigned-job creatures are all visually distinct at 1280x720. The player can identify creature states and terrain boundaries at a glance. Score 0 if elements blend together or creature states are indistinguishable.

HUD shows essential information: job toolbar with remaining counts, creatures saved vs quota, creatures currently alive, release rate control, and level identity. All information is persistent and readable during gameplay. Score 0 if no toolbar or progress information is visible.

Title screen, level select, and results screens are present with styled navigation. Results show save percentage and star rating. Pause functionality allows planning without time pressure. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay with no navigation.

The game has a coherent factory-industrial art direction: terrain, creatures, hazards, UI, and backgrounds share a consistent visual language with mechanical textures and a warm industrial palette. Score 0 if visuals are raw default controls or unthemed rectangles. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Creatures are animated characters with walking cycles, job-specific animations (digging motion, building motion, blocking pose), and death reactions. Terrain has textured tiles and hazards have mechanical detail. Score 0 if creatures are plain circles and terrain is flat fills.

Creature actions, terrain modification, hazard triggers, and level transitions have polished animation: digging shows debris particles, building shows tile placement, death has reaction effects, and screen transitions are smooth. Score 0 if all state changes are instant snaps.
